candidates.title: Jailbreak
candidates.reason: A Cambodian martial-arts action film in which police escorting a witness become trapped in a prison riot. Whole-film reviews describe an introductory escort/setup followed by repeated fights across cells and corridors, including mob confrontations, improvised weapons and one-on-one duels. Action recurs for much of the film, but Film Combat Syndicate notes intervals between set pieces and Tilt Magazine describes long pauses, so density is not treated as near-continuous. Screen Anarchy and Heroic Cinema praise the mobile camera and clearly staged bokator choreography; Heroic Cinema says no gun is fired on screen. Limitations include repeated groups-of-inmates fight beats, one-building setting, weak characterization, uneven acting and comic interruptions. Repetition, limited action variety and limited setting variety are recorded independently of the strong physical choreography. Descriptive DNA only; no ranking or publication conclusion.

candidates.title: The Roundup: Punishment
candidates.reason: A 109-minute South Korean police action-comedy about an illegal online gambling syndicate, with an investigation spanning Seoul and the Philippines. Screen Daily describes a brisk but formulaic mixture of police procedure, humor and fights, while RogerEbert.com details a pursuit and the final confrontation and criticizes underpowered action and generic characterization. AsianMovieWeb describes a notable knife fight involving the villain and recurring heavy-handed boxing-style clashes, but also investigative and comic passages. Consequently the whole-film action density is moderate-to-high rather than continuous; intense individual melee scenes do not substitute for density. The cybercrime investigation and international locations add some variety, while repetition of the series formula, thin supporting roles and a less distinctive finale are limitations. The villain's former military background does not make this a military-operation film, and unsanctioned boxing-style punches are not sports fighting. Descriptive DNA only; no final eligibility or score is inferred.

research_rejections.title: Revenger
research_rejections.reason: A whole-film AsianMovieWeb review reports a prolonged action-light opening, with fighting only accelerating around the 30-minute mark and further lengthy pauses. Its attractive choreography alone is insufficient evidence of sustained action density, so it is not advanced as a candidate.

research_rejections.title: One Percenter
research_rejections.reason: Rotten Tomatoes review excerpts describe an extended setup that takes too long to begin and repetitive action beats. Whole-runtime density remains insufficiently established for a confident candidate despite the action-star-versus-yakuza premise.
